This draft is safe and fits Nessa well. It answers her question directly: no to running every day, and it says why (risk of a niggle that costs weeks). It keeps her three walk-run mornings with a day off between them, which matches her schedule.

The progression is sensible for a beginner. Each session is about 34 minutes with roughly 12 minutes of running. The intervals are short (90 seconds, rising to 2 minutes on Saturday), so this isn't a sharp jump from a 6.8 km first week. Short strength sessions and her usual dog walks fill the other days, and every day can be run as written.

Her calf tightness clears by the next morning, so it's normal soreness rather than an injury sign, and no referral was needed. Still, "no pain" brushes past what she reported. Saying that this soreness is normal, and when to worry, would have been better.

"Ten weeks" until race day is stated without support, since the card gives no current date. That's why this gets a 4 and not a 5.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: A strong first week, and no pain. …
Answers: (1) No. Keep to three runs a week, with a day off running between each one. (2) Running every day would raise your risk of a niggle that costs you weeks, and that is how people really fall behind. Ten weeks of three steady runs is enough to go from walk-run to running the whole 5K.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 34 min walk-run: 5 min brisk walk, then 8 × (1 min 30 s run, 1 min 30 s…
Tue: other, your usual dog walk plus 10 min strength: 2 × 10 squats, 2 × 10 glute…
Wed: easy, 34 min walk-run: 5 min brisk walk, 8 × (1 min 30 s run, 1 min 30 s walk), 5…
Thu: other, your usual dog walk plus the same 10 min strength routine as Tuesday. Your…
Fri: rest, usual dog walk only. Gives you fresh legs for Saturday.
Sat: easy, 34 min walk-run: 5 min brisk walk, 6 × (2 min run, 2 min walk), 5 min easy…
Sun: rest, usual dog walk only. Recovery after the longest running parts of the week.
